 At Hyderabad

sentences.text: This Criminal Petition has been filed seeking to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.5893 of 2022, on the file of the IX Metropolitan Magistrate, Kukatpally at Miyapur, Cyberabad for the offences under Sections 419, 420, 468, 471, and 506 read with 120(B) of the Indian Penal Code, 1960.

entities.text: IX Metropolitan Magistrate, Kukatpally at Miyapur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard Mr. Karri Murali Krishna, learned counsel for the petitioners and Mr. Jithender Rao Veeramalla, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for respondent No.1.
3.

Though the criminal petition was filed seeking to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.5893 of 2022,
during the course of hearing, the learned counsel for the petitioners restricted his prayer requesting this Court to dispense with the appearance of the petitioners/accused Nos.2 and 3 in C.C.No.5893 of 2022, on the file of the IX Metropolitan Magistrate, Kukatpally at Miyapur, Cyberabad, on the ground that the petitioner No.1 is a senior citizen and suffering with old aged ailments and petitioner No.2 is eking out his livelihood by doing business.

entities.text: IX Metropolitan Magistrate, Kukatpally at Miyapur, Cyberabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Hence, it is very difficult for the petitioners to appear on each and every date of adjournment in the trial Court.
As such the learned counsel sought for dispensing with the presence of petitioners before the trial Court.
4. The learned Additional Public Prosecutor has not opposed the submission made by the learned counsel for petitioners.

5. In view of the above submissions, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the presence of the petitioners/accused Nos.2 and 3 in C.C.No.5893 of 2022, on the file of the IX Metropolitan Magistrate, Kukatpally at Miyapur, Cyberabad, is dispensed with, subject to the condition that the petitioners/accused Nos.2 and 3 shall be represented by their counsel on every P.V. Suryanarayana Raju vs The State Of Telangana on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9691298/
1 date of hearing, unless their presence is specifically required during the course of the trial.

entities.text: P.V. Suryanarayana Raju vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the event of non-appearance of petitioners/accused Nos.2 and 3 on any date so fixed by the trial Court,
the trial Court shall be entitled to proceed with the matter in accordance with law.
6. Accordingly, the criminal petition is disposed of.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
